newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban airliner crash claims 44, 20 bodies recovered.
newsitem.headline: Cuban airliner crash claims 44, 20 bodies recovered.

text.p: Convinced there were no survivors, Cuban authorities continued late on Saturday a search for bodies of 44 people killed in an airliner crash off eastern Cuba late on Friday.

There were eight foreigners -- six Spaniards and two Brazilians -- on the Cubana de Aviacion An-24 plane which plunged into the sea minutes after taking off on a late evening domestic flight from Santiago to Havana.
The statement said 20 bodies had been recovered in a search involving coast guard cutters, air force planes, fishing boats and frogmen. These bodies were currently being identified, it added.
Patrols would continue around the area of the crash site in the hope of recovering more bodies, the statement said.
There was no indication yet of what caused flight 787 to crash. The An-24, a Soviet-made Antonov, is a twin-engined turbo-prop plane.
The civil aviation institute said earlier that it had set up a state commission to investigate causes of the accident. The plane was flying with 39 passengers and five crew.

Santiago de Cuba, the island's second-largest city, is about 530 miles (850 km) southeast of Havana. One of Cuba's oldest cities, it is a popular destination for foreign tourists interested in Cuba's culture and history.
The Communist-ruled island's worst airline disaster was in September 1989, when 126 people were killed when a Cuban airlines plane crashed near Havana.
